title: 1:1 impact storyboard — manager prep (Aisha)
content:
1:1 Impact Storyboard — quick read (top of page)
Date: 2026-03-05
Audience: Manager (prep), self-reflection notes, light share in meeting

OBJECTIVE
- Primary: Make the case for sustained impact and a promotion trajectory conversation in Q2.
- Secondary: Get alignment on support needs (stretch project, sponsor intros, deferral on two operational tasks).

WORKING NARRATIVE (elevator)
- Over the last 6 months I rebuilt the onboarding checklist and cross-team hiring rubric that reduced new-hire ramp time by ~18%. I led the execution of two hiring sprints (Eng + DX) and improved offer-to-accept time by 9 days through refined interview loops and scorecard discipline. My next step is to run a small cross-functional playbook project to codify role families and create manager enablement for promotion calibration.

KEY METRICS TO SHARE (evidence-oriented)
- New-hire ramp (metric): baseline 12 weeks -> now 9.8 weeks (goal 8 weeks). Data source: HR dashboard weekly export (OKR tracker).
- Offer acceptance delta: average offer->accept 21 days -> 12 days after loop changes. (Jira: HR-337 contains timeline)
- Manager satisfaction (pulse): pilot cohort N=7 -> average 4.3/5 on enablement survey.

TOP 3 WINS (last 6 weeks)
1) Onboarding checklist revamp shipped (PR: github:pr/1423) — fewer missing training steps, positive notes from hiring managers.
2) Interview rubric workshop with Eng leads — resulted in standardized scorecards for IC2-IC4.
3) Launched pilot mentor pairing for XFN new hires (pilot cohort feedback 4.4/5).

OPEN RISKS / QUESTIONS
- Risk: I am spending ~30% of time on operational hiring logistics (scheduling, ad-hoc interviews) which is starving strategic time.
  - Ask: Can we reassign scheduling to recruiting ops or hire a part-time coordinator?
- Risk: Need a sponsor for cross-functional promotion calibration; current stakeholders are overloaded.
  - Ask: Intro to VP People or Sr Manager who can champion the project.

PROBING AGENDA (things I want feedback on)
- Is the direction of the role-family playbook aligned with org priorities? (prioritization, audience)
- Sign-off criteria for me to be recommended for promotion: what signals would you like to see in Q2? (impact, autonomy, mentorship)
- How would you advise me to balance tactical hiring work vs. strategic productization of playbooks?

SPECIFIC REQUESTS (ask the manager)
- Short-term: 8 hours/week backfill on scheduling for 8 weeks (reassign to recruiter ops).
- Mid-term: Sponsor intro to VP People for the role-family playbook by March 20.
- Coaching: 3 x 30-minute calibration sessions with you before Q2 calibration (April).

DETAILED EVIDENCE / NOTES (copy-paste snippets to share if asked)
- Quote from hiring manager (Lina): "Onboarding changes cut the time-to-first-code in half for two recent hires — really tangible improvement."
- Pilot survey notes: "Mentor pairing accelerated context adoption, but mentors wanted a 15-min weekly sync template"
- Slack thread: #hiring-ops: see conversation on interview rubric v3 (link in linked_artifacts).

GROWTH AREAS I AM WORKING ON
- Delegation: clear task handoffs, creating checklists, and runbooks for recurring ops tasks.
- Strategic storytelling: succinctly packaging impact for exec eyes (1-slide narrative).
- Cross-team influence: more frequent stakeholder syncs and pre-read circulation.

CAREER PITCH (30s)
- "I drive operational changes that free up engineering time and improve hire quality. I'm ready to own the playbooks and the promotion calibration process so we can scale managers and reduce variability across teams."

NEXT 3 ACTIONS (me)
1) Draft role-family playbook outline v0 — due 2026-03-15 (share for initial review).
2) Send a short list of potential scheduling backfills to Recruiting Ops by 2026-03-09.
3) Prepare a 1-slide impact summary for our 3/18 1:1 — include the three metrics above and the single ask.

NOTES TO SELF (scratch)
- Keep data light in 1:1 — manager prefers top-line + one supporting datapoint.
- Bring proposed sponsor names, not just need.
- Be explicit about timeline for promotion expectations.
- If manager pushes back on sponsor, ask for alternative routes (skip-level email intro, HR partnership).

END
